items.title: OMNIRAY: LY4257496 Study in GRPR-Positive Advanced Cancers Including Prostate
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is testing LY4257496, a new drug targeting a protein called GRPR found in several cancers including prostate cancer. The study evaluates the drug alone and combined with standard treatments. Participants with advanced GRPR-positive cancers can join. The trial could last up to 36 weeks.

items.title: BPX-601 CAR T-Cell Therapy for Recurrent Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study tests BPX-601, a personalized CAR-T cell therapy made from a patient's own immune cells, for advanced prostate cancer that has returned or spread. The study will determine the best dose and examine side effects. It aims to see how well these engineered cells can destroy prostate cancer. The trial is not yet recruiting patients.

items.title: AMG 509 Study in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates AMG 509 alone and combined with standard hormone therapies (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study examines safety, how the drug is processed by the body, and early signs of effectiveness. Currently recruiting patients for specific expansion cohorts.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, alone and with other treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will identify safe doses when combined with other therapies and measure PSA levels and side effects. It is currently recruiting participants.

items.title: Comparing PSMA and Bone Scan PET Imaging in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 study compares two types of PET scans for detecting metastatic prostate cancer sites: 18F-DCFPyL (PSMA-targeted) versus 18F-NaF (bone-targeted). The goal is to determine which imaging method better identifies cancer spread. The trial is active but no longer recruiting new participants.

items.title: TRC003 for Progressive PSMA-Positive Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates TRC003, a PSMA-targeted therapy, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have already received hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The study will test three different doses across 90 participants and assess safety, effectiveness, and how the body processes the drug. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Versus Chemotherapy in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 study compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) to chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The primary goal is to determine if patients live longer overall and have longer periods without cancer growth when receiving I-DXd. This is a large, recruiting trial comparing against current standard chemotherapy.

items.title: Cabozantinib, Nivolumab, and Ipilimumab for Rare Genitourinary Tumors
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests combining cabozantinib (targeted therapy) with nivolumab and ipilimumab (immunotherapies) for rare genitourinary tumors including some prostate cancers. The study examines whether this triple combination works better than single agents alone. Currently recruiting patients with rare GU tumors lacking other treatment options.

items.title: Real-World Study: Darolutamide Plus Hormone Therapy in Germany
items.summary: This observational study tracks how well darolutamide combined with hormone therapy works for men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer in routine German medical practice. It collects real-world data on effectiveness and side effects outside of controlled clinical trials. Currently recruiting participants.

items.title: Blood Collection for Prostate Cancer Genetics Research
items.summary: This study collects blood samples from prostate cancer patients to identify genetic differences that may explain why some cancers become resistant to hormone therapy. The research aims to find gene variations associated with progression to androgen-independent disease. Samples are collected from participants in NCI prostate cancer protocols.

items.title: TD001 Safety Study in PSMA-Positive Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates TD001, a PSMA-targeted antibody-drug conjugate, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study examines safety, drug levels in the body, and early signs of tumor response. Currently recruiting participants with PSMA-positive tumors.

items.title: Phase 3: AZD2265 Versus Standard Care in PSMA-Positive mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares AZD2265 to standard treatments in PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will measure if AZD2265 extends time without cancer growth and overall survival compared to current therapies. This is a large recruiting trial testing a new PSMA-targeted therapy.

items.title: Radiation Therapy for Recurrent or Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies shorter radiation therapy schedules (hypofractionated proton therapy or IMRT) for prostate cancer that has returned or spread to limited sites after initial treatment. The goal is to determine if fewer, higher doses of radiation can be as effective with fewer side effects. The trial is active but not recruiting.

items.title: Cediranib Plus Olaparib Versus Olaparib Alone in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial compares combination therapy (olaparib plus cediranib) to olaparib alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Olaparib is a PARP inhibitor that prevents cancer cells from repairing DNA damage. The study examines whether adding cediranib improves outcomes. The trial is active but not recruiting.

items.title: INR731 Safety Study in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests INR731 alone and combined with standard hormone therapies (androgen receptor pathway inhibitors) in metastatic prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety, how the drug is processed, and early effectiveness signals. Currently recruiting participants.

items.title: Phase 3: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide to enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients who haven't received prior hormone therapy intensification. The study tests whether adding mevrometostat improves outcomes over standard enzalutamide treatment. Currently recruiting.

items.title: PDS01ADC Combinations in Metastatic Castration-Sensitive and Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study tests PDS01ADC (an antibody-drug conjugate) combined with docetaxel and abiraterone in metastatic castration-sensitive disease, and PDS01ADC with docetaxel in castration-resistant disease. The goal is to determine if these combinations safely delay cancer progression. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Phase 3: Opevesostat Versus Alternative Hormone Therapy in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares opevesostat to switching to a different standard hormone therapy (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients previously treated with one hormone agent. The study measures time without cancer growth and tests effectiveness in patients with and without specific gene mutations. Currently recruiting.

items.title: AAA817 After Lutetium-177-PSMA Therapy in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2/3 trial tests AAA817 versus standard care in patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose disease progressed after Lutetium-177-PSMA radioligand therapy. It evaluates treatment options for patients who have already received hormone therapy, chemotherapy, and PSMA-targeted radiation. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Phase 3: Lutetium-177 PSMA Versus Observation in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 study compares Lutetium-177 vipivotide tetraxetan (PSMA radioligand therapy) to observation in oligometastatic prostate cancer patients after primary treatment. The goal is to control cancer recurrence and delay hormone therapy while preserving quality of life. This tests PSMA therapy in earlier-stage disease. Currently recruiting.

items.title: IL-12-Enhanced Human PSMA-CAR T Cells for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research develops improved PSMA-targeted CAR T-cell therapy using a fully human antibody design combined with IL-12 to enhance immune response. The modified cells showed increased expansion, better tumor killing, and improved immune signaling in laboratory studies. This represents an advance in making CAR-T therapy safer and more effective for prostate cancer.

items.title: 2025 Top Advances: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review summarizes major 2025 advances in radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer, including PSMA-targeted treatments. The field has evolved from pain management with radium-223 to cancer-directed therapies that extend survival. These targeted radiation treatments represent a rapidly advancing area in metastatic prostate cancer management.

items.title: AI Biomarkers Predict Hormone Therapy Response and Identify mTOR Target
items.summary: This multicenter study used artificial intelligence to identify 13 cellular biomarkers from prostate biopsy images that accurately predict response to hormone therapy plus enzalutamide. The biomarkers successfully identified treatment responders versus non-responders across multiple hospitals. The study also found that targeting mTOR may help patients whose cancer is resistant to hormone therapy.

items.title: Optimizing Care in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.source: American Society of Clinical Oncology educational book. American Society of Clinical Oncology. Annual Meeting
items.summary: This clinical guide presents a framework for managing metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer using multiple treatment types including hormone therapies, chemotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and radioisotopes. The review emphasizes integrating molecular testing, imaging, and supportive care to guide treatment decisions as earlier intensification creates more complex treatment sequencing challenges.

items.title: Novel Therapies Beyond Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review examines emerging treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer when hormone therapy fails, including PARP inhibitors for DNA repair defects, PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy, immunotherapies, and antibody-drug conjugates. The article discusses how genetic testing and PSMA imaging can guide treatment selection for resistant disease.

items.title: Prognostic Factors for PSMA Radioligand Therapy in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis identifies factors that predict outcomes in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients treated with PSMA radioligand therapy. The study synthesized data on clinical, blood test, and imaging features associated with progression-free and overall survival to help guide patient selection for PSMA therapy.

items.title: PSA Kinetics Predict Outcomes in Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This real-world study of 352 patients examined how PSA changes predict outcomes in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer treated with upfront hormone therapy intensification. Achieving very low PSA levels (nadir ≤0.02) and >99% PSA decline were strongly associated with longer time to castration resistance and better survival.

items.title: NADIR Model Performance in Real-World Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study validated the NADIR prediction model in 186 real-world patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer receiving hormone therapy intensification. The model, originally developed from clinical trials, accurately predicted which patients would achieve favorable early PSA responses (≤0.2 ng/mL within 6 months) in routine practice.

items.title: Real-World Comparison of Darolutamide, Apalutamide, and Enzalutamide in Non-Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Japanese multicenter study compared 343 patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer treated with darolutamide, apalutamide, or enzalutamide. After adjusting for baseline differences, darolutamide showed better treatment persistence and outcomes. The study provides real-world comparative effectiveness data for these three hormone therapies.

items.title: Circulating Tumor DNA Predicts Survival in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 13 studies involving 18,575 patients found that detectable circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in blood predicts significantly worse progression-free survival and overall survival in metastatic prostate cancer. The study demonstrates ctDNA's value as a minimally invasive biomarker for prognosis and potentially treatment monitoring.

items.title: Review: Reducing Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review examines ongoing studies testing whether newer hormone therapies (androgen receptor pathway inhibitors) can effectively treat metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer while minimizing or avoiding traditional androgen deprivation therapy. The goal is to maintain cancer control while reducing side effects like cardiovascular disease, bone loss, and cognitive impairment.

items.title: Cabazitaxel Versus Second Hormone Therapy After Docetaxel in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This real-world study of 517 heavily pretreated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients compared survival outcomes between cabazitaxel chemotherapy and switching to another hormone therapy after prior docetaxel and hormone treatment. Cabazitaxel was more commonly used and in later treatment lines than subsequent hormone therapies.

items.title: Simple Two-Factor Score Predicts Outcomes in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed a bedside prognostic score combining performance status and aggressive metastatic burden to predict outcomes in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. This simple tool helps identify patients with worse prognosis who may need more intensive initial treatment. The score was developed and validated in a real-world cohort.

items.title: SPOP Mutations and Treatment Outcomes in Veterans With Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This large Veterans Affairs study examined 984 men with SPOP-mutated prostate cancer, a genetic subtype that may be especially sensitive to hormone therapies. Most veterans received intensive hormone therapy and showed favorable survival outcomes. SPOP mutations occur in 5-15% of prostate cancers and affect androgen receptor signaling.

items.title: Triplet Versus Doublet Therapy in High-Volume Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Japanese registry study compared triplet therapy (hormone therapy, docetaxel, and androgen receptor inhibitor) to doublet therapy (hormone therapy and androgen receptor inhibitor) in 140 patients with high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The analysis used advanced statistical methods and exploratory combination with phase 3 trial data.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Resistance in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed a novel drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT proteins to overcome treatment resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Compound 21d was identified as particularly effective. This dual-targeting approach addresses resistance mechanisms driven by c-MYC elevation when AKT inhibitors are used alone.
